doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Artistic leader versus business leader in co-led bands
summary: Young and Brown agree Thad Jones and John Clayton were the artistic leaders while Mel Lewis and Jeff Hamilton handled business.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So, again, I think what I‘m trying to say is, let‘s go back and we think of the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band, this is one of the first bands that‘s co-lead, you know, you

got a trumpet player and you got a drummer leading a big band. Before that you had, either Count Basie as a leader, you had Jimmie Lunceford as a leader, you had all these other single leaders, this is the first time you‘re working with a co-lead big band. Was there any difference when they have two leaders of a band?

I guess it was different, but it didn‘t… you kind of wondered who, who was the boss in the band like that, I mean, you wondered, but it‘s not one of those guys is was the leader, that‘s the funny thing. Thad Jones was the leader that Mel Lewis and Thad Jones‘s band, Thad Jones was the leader. Mel Jones…
Mel Lewis.

Mel took the business and everything, but the leader was Thad. That‘s the same thing in this band. The leader is John Clayton. Jeff Hamilton, they do business and Jeff… but the leader is John Clayton. Now, I hope that isn‘t saying the wrong thing about the men, you know what I‘m saying.
No, but it clarifies the roles that each person is playing as a leader.
What did you say?

I said, this clarifies the role that each person plays as a leader, one sounds more like an artistic director and the other one sounds more like a managing or… administrative director. So one seems to have, like in Thad Jones, seemed to be more the artistic director of the band, he would make all the artistic decisions, where as maybe Mel Lewis handled more of the business and not so many of the artistic decisions of the band. Sounds like that‘s what you‘re saying also about the Clayton-Hamilton band. That John Clayton is the artistic director. He‘s the creative force, or the main creative force, and that Jeff Hamilton handles the business and is supportive in that role.
That‘s true.
Okay.
That‘s right. That‘s about the way it is.
Okay.

John puts a lot of stuff on Jeff and on Jim, I mean you know, he don‘t do everything, but he don‘t have to he‘s got three leaders. You see what I‘m saying, there‘s three of them. So, that takes a lot of weight off of him. I never thought about that, but it does. Because I know Jeff does a lot of things, Jeff, Jeff Hamilton I‘m talking about, he
takes a lot of… they all three handle the band very good, and it runs good, it runs easy, the business… the business part of the band.
Was the business also in the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band? Was the business together? Was it good?

Yeah, well it‘s been long, it‘s been so many years, I‘ve got so many years that have passed between them, I don‘t remember everything, but it was very good like that too. Mel, Mel did a lot of the pencil work. Thad did other things now that I think about it. Mel was…
Handling the business.
Handling the business, and I could be wrong about that, but I don‘t think so.
Well, that was what you experienced, that‘s what you witnessed.
Yeah, that‘s what I experienced when I was there.
